newsitem.title: INDIA: India Hind Motor to launch rural vehicle.
newsitem.headline: India Hind Motor to launch rural vehicle.

text.p: India's Hindustan Motors Ltd said on Tuesday it would introduce a 300,000 rupee ($8,400) vehicle aimed at rural India in April 1998.

"The Hindustan Motors' Rural Transport Vehicle (RTV) will cater to India's 500,000 villages where roads are a luxury, and where consumers want a vehicle that can move people and goods with equal ease," R. Santhanam, Hindustan Motors' executive vice president, told a news conference.

"The RTV can achieve a top speed of 90 km (per hour) on the road, and go as slow as five km (per hour) on rough terrain, without any problem. It will go 11 to 12 km to a litre of diesel, making it economical to operate," he said.
He said the firm had spent 400 million rupees in developing the vehicle. "We commissioned Australia's Oka Motor Co Ltd to design the vehicle two-and-a-half years ago," he said.
The vehicle will run on a two-litre Isuzu Motors Ltd diesel engine, manufactured by Hindustan Motors for its Ambassador cars.
Santhanam said Hindustan Motors would make about 600 RTVs a month in the first 15 months of production, and would then decide on whether to increase capacity.
He said the RTV would be manufactured at the firm's engine and gearbox plant near the city of Indore, in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh.
The company will also consider exporting the vehicle, especially to countries such as Vietnam and Indonesia, Santhanam said.
He said the RTV was part of the company's strategy to develop three types of products for the Indian market.

Hindustan Motors is targeting the Lancer, to be produced from June 1998 under licence from Mitsubishi Motor Corp of Japan, at car buyers in the five big cities of Delhi, Bombay, Madras, Calcutta and Bangalore, and state capitals.
For consumers in smaller towns, it has its Contessa and Ambassador models, and for those in villages it has the four-wheel drive Trekker and the RTV.
The Association of Indian Automobile Manufacturers estimates that vehicle production will top a million units by 2000, up from 404,040 units in 1996/97 (April-March). ($ = 35.7 Indian Rupees)
